story.title: Story 3: Message Projection and Token Estimates

result.planSummary: Fixed F-03-002. openThreadDatabase now performs an identity check before any migration runs: a read-only probe (so the probe itself cannot mutate an invalid file) requires schema version >= 1, a thread_metadata table, and the metadata singleton row that thread creation writes transactionally. Files failing the check — an empty database, an unrelated SQLite database, a non-database file — are rejected as caller_error/thread_not_found ('exists but is not an lhc thread file') with no lhc tables created and user_version untouched; SQLite's 'not a database' refusal is classified as the same identity failure, while other open errors remain system_error. The opener's signature changed to OpResult<DatabaseSync> so the rejection flows through the standard result contract, and all three call sites (runMessageEvents, runListEvents, listMessages) propagate it. Valid Story 2 user_version=1 files pass the check (they carry the metadata row) and still migrate lazily to v2, so F-03-001 behavior is preserved — all prior migration tests stay green. Three focused tests prove rejection-without-mutation for an existing empty file (verifier's exact probe), an unrelated SQLite database with foreign data, and a plain text file.

changedFiles.reason: Added validateThreadFile (read-only identity probe: version >= 1, thread_metadata table, singleton row) run before migrations; openThreadDatabase now returns OpResult<DatabaseSync>, rejecting non-thread files as caller_error/thread_not_found and wrapping environment failures as system_error
runMessageEvents and runListEvents consume the opener's OpResult, returning the rejection instead of opening/migrating arbitrary files
listMessages consumes the opener's OpResult, so read-back on a non-thread file fails instead of adopting the file

Added an F-03-002 describe block: three rejection tests asserting error class/code and, below the SDK, unchanged user_version, no lhc tables created, foreign data and raw bytes intact; F-03-001 tests unchanged above it
Re-recorded thread-migration.test.ts hash after appending the F-03-002 tests

added: test/thread-migration.test.ts: listMessages against an existing empty database file fails with caller_error/thread_not_found, user_version stays 0, no tables created (the verifier's exact F-03-002 probe)
test/thread-migration.test.ts: messageEvents against an unrelated SQLite database fails, creates no lhc tables, leaves user_version at 0 and the foreign rows intact
test/thread-migration.test.ts: a non-SQLite text file is rejected as caller_error/thread_not_found by both listMessages and messageEvents with its bytes byte-identical afterward

findingsFixed: F-03-002: the lazy opener no longer creates lhc schema on, or returns successful read-back from, arbitrary existing files — a read-only identity probe (schema version >= 1 plus the thread_metadata singleton) gates migration, invalid existing files are rejected as caller_error/thread_not_found without any mutation, and Story 2 user_version=1 files still migrate lazily (all F-03-001 tests remain green)
findingsSurfaced: The 'not a database' classification relies on SQLite's error message text to distinguish identity failures from environment failures; node:sqlite exposes no stable error code for SQLITE_NOTADB, so a wording change in a future Node release would downgrade that case to system_error (still a rejection, never adoption) — worth a glance when bumping the Node engine

thread_not_found is reused for 'exists but is not a thread file' because the epic's error-code set is closed; the reason string distinguishes the cases. If operators need to tell them apart programmatically, a dedicated code would be a vocabulary addition for a future story
The read-only probe adds one extra open per SDK operation on a thread file; negligible at v1 scale, and it is the only way to guarantee the probe itself cannot mutate an invalid file

result.recommendedNextStep: Re-verify F-03-002 with the new rejection tests (the original empty-file probe now returns caller_error/thread_not_found with user_version still 0 and no tables); F-03-001 coverage is unchanged and green. Then proceed to Story 4, whose turn tables should land as a version-3 migration behind the same validated opener.
